description:
matches_dns_san at pkix-identity/src/lib.rs:644 rejects wildcard SANs of the form '*.<single-label>' (no further dot after the wildcard label) — e.g. '*.com'. The module rustdoc and the san_wildcard_rejects_single_label_tld test both lock this in.

A future contributor or commenter will suggest 'this is a public-suffix-list concern, not the validator's job — remove this'. They will cite the README which says PSL is out of scope.

Defend: this is a STRUCTURAL check, not a PSL lookup. It blocks the most catastrophic wildcard misuse (*.com matching any .com) without bringing in PSL data. It is universally safe — there is no legitimate use case for '*.com' style wildcards. webpki and the major browsers all apply equivalent structural restrictions independent of PSL. The check is cheap, ASCII-only, and does not regress on legitimate '*.foo.example.com' patterns. Removing it would be a security regression masquerading as scope discipline.
title: Decision: wildcard *.<single-label> structurally rejected as defense-in-depth against PSL
